Hi team,

We saw a spike of failures shortly after the privately scheduled control-plane upgrade in our VPC at ~03:05 UTC. Symptoms: persistent 503s from the inference endpoint, sporadic TLS handshake errors in our sidecar logs, and agent heartbeats dropping for ~20% of nodes. The issues started around 03:10 UTC and persisted with intermittent recovery until ~07:00 UTC.

Attached is a small sample of our sidecar logs and a screenshot of the gateway metrics. Can you confirm whether the upgrade included any OS/kernel or TLS stack changes? We need an RCA and short-term mitigation — our support team is seeing customer impact.

From: evelyn_hart@redwood.com

Date: Tue, 15 Sep 2026 09:48:10 -0700
Subject: INTERNAL: initial SRE triage notes (privatenet upgrade)

Internal-only notes (summary to share w/ customer once we have a short mitigation):
- Timeline: 02:58 UTC - control-plane rolling upgrade initiated (coordinated with MedCore). 03:05–03:12 UTC - spike in TLS handshake failures; 03:10 UTC - first agent heartbeat drop seen (controlplane -> agent keepalives timed out).
- Root-candidate: kernel backported patch in the host image included a change to TCP delayed ack behavior + updated OpenSSL minor version. Under our sustained connection pattern (many short-lived TLS sessions for agent gossip), we observed increased SYN/ACK timeouts on ~18 of 90 nodes (20% hit).
- Correlation: nodes with older NIC firmware saw higher RTT variance; combined with the OpenSSL minor bump resulted in increased renegotiation attempts and ephemeral session failures.

Immediate mitigations applied (we pushed these at ~04:15 UTC):
1) Rolled back the OpenSSL minor package on a canary subset (10 nodes) — observed heartbeat recovery within ~90s.
2) Adjusted control-plane keepalive to a slightly longer interval and increased TLS handshake timeout to reduce premature aborts.
3) Placed a temporary routing bypass to avoid a noisy NAT gateway in two AZs.

Next steps we recommend for MedCore (short window patch):
- Keep the temporary routing bypass in place for 24 hours while we stage a full rollback across the fleet.
- Share list of nodes that must remain isolated for compliance so we don’t auto-roll them back.
- Prepare for a concerted rollback window; we can do a full rollback within 6 hours of approval.

I’m attaching diffs we recorded between pre/post-upgrade control-plane configs. I’ll join the 10:00 PDT bridge with a short runbook and will record the session.

Evelyn Hart
SRE Manager, Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Privatenet upgrade: remediation plan and temporary mitigations

Sanjay / Priya — thank you again for the patience on the bridge. Following the triage (notes below) we propose the following immediate remediation plan: 

1) Short-term (recommended immediately):
   - Keep the routing bypass in place for the two affected AZs (you already have the toggle in your console). This prevents the noisy NAT from exacerbating timeouts.
   - Apply the control-plane keepalive relax (we pushed a change server-side; no agent restart required).

2) Medium-term (requires approval): Full rollback of the OpenSSL minor update across the private fleet. Expected impact: rolling rollback with ~5–10 minute disruption per host as we re-provision shared libs. We can run a canary then proceed fleet-wide. Total ETA after approval: ~6 hours.

3) Permanent fix: coordinate with our image team to backport a NIC firmware compatibility shim and validate the OpenSSL patch matrix. Target: next scheduled maintenance window (we will propose dates).

Artifacts provided: orchestration logs and a config diff (attached). We’ve created JIRA INC-4721 to track the rollback and postmortem; I’ll link the final RCA here once complete.

Action items for MedCore:
- Confirm approval for the medium-term rollback (reply with APPROVE to this thread).
- Provide list of nodes that cannot be touched for compliance.

We’ll be on the bridge for the next hour and will execute the canary rollback on approval.

Regards,
Nikhil Sharma
Support Engineering Lead, Redwood Inference
